met_analysis:
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northwest Bay of Bengal adjoining west Bengal north Odisha coast lies over South Bangladesh adjoining Gangetic West Bengal at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The trough now runs from northwest Bay of Bengal to East Uttar Pradesh across north Odisha, Jharkhand and southwest Bihar at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over central Pakistan & neighbourhoodbetween 0.9 & 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over east Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over east Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood at 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar & adjoining south Tamil Nadu coast at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Arabian Sea adjoining south Kerala coast lies over South Kerala & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over Himachal Pradesh & adjoining north Haryana between 1.5 to 5.8 km above mean sea level persists, with a trough aloft in upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 77°E to the north of Lat. 27°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation south Andaman Sea & neighbourhood extending upto 9.4 km above mean sea level persists. Under its influence, a low-pressure area is likely to form over the Southeast Bay of Bengal around 13th October.
